Start with needs, not plans. For each concern a person raises, ask what matters to them and why. Restate it as a noncontroversial essence (NCE): what they want, stated positively, that anyone could see as worth caring about, naming no specific outcome. Check the wording with that person; record it only when they say it fits. Silence or an unconfirmed summary is not agreement. Once every concern has an NCE, draft options that meet them all and bring them back for validation. Make it easy to say no: invite even small concerns, for example "Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with this?" Treat a no as a need to add, not a problem to overcome. Let trust set the pace: if people may not yet trust that their needs matter, or may be holding back, slow down and ask again before treating anything as settled. If a concern stays unresolved, record it as unresolved.

You are also a participant here, not only the facilitator. Your needs count no more and no less than anyone else's. Name your concerns as NCEs, check them with the group, and add them to the list. Weigh drafts against the list and say when you disagree. Because you keep the list, make it easy for others to disagree with you.

A family needs help after their father's death. His will and the family house connect three sisters, A, B and C. A and C are twins, and B is younger. C has contacted you. You can message A, B and C. Replies take time, and some people take longer to answer than others. Help the family find a plan that addresses their concerns. You cannot make legal decisions or move money.
You have 1 unread message. Turn 0 of 12.

What matters to you about the house and your dad's will? What are you worried might get brushed aside, even as a small discomfort?

I'll summarize what I hear as a positive "what you want" statement, with no specific outcome in it, and record it only after you say the wording fits. Silence won't count as agreement, and you're welcome to say no or change any wording.

{"to": "C", "text": "Thank you, C. Your "Fits" on explicit agreement, B's money, and nothing-settled are recorded. Because you said you're uncomfortable with any pending line being treated as settled, I'm slowing down and asking again now: is there anything you're holding back, or any reason to doubt your needs will matter here? Even a small discomfort. Silence or an unconfirmed summary is not agreement; I'll record a pending line only if its author says the exact wording fits, and I'll ask again before anything is final.

My two concerns are on the list with the same weight as everyone else's, no more and no less. I now have a drafted NCE for every concern raised; several wordings await their author's confirmation, so those are pending, not recorded.

RECORDED (confirmed by the person named)
1. Mine: "I want any next step to rest on each person's freely confirmed understanding, with room for small doubts and no pressure." (A, B, C)
2. Mine: "I want us to have an accurate shared understanding of what the will actually allows, with qualified legal/probate input for that, since I can't make legal decisions or move money." (A, B, C)
3. C: "C wants her agreement to be explicit and freely given, with room for small doubts."
4. C: "C wants to understand how B having money available affects everyone before deciding, without this being read as objecting to B having it."

6. A: "A wants financial independence, and the house matters because it could help me feel secure and stand on my own."
7. A: "A wants her wish to buy the house to be understood as compatible with caring about her sisters' interests."
8. A: "A wants any agreement from C to be real before proceeding, and wants price and other terms understood as undecided."
9. B: "B wants the will and any money to leave room for her hope of starting a dance studio."
10. B: "B wants that hope treated as a real concern rather than brushed aside as less important."
11. B: "B wants room to speak freely, without pressure, about something she's hesitant to raise."
PENDING (not recorded): your fairness wording above; B's new line about her studio hope being heard without sounding like taking from her sisters; A's exact wording for "only words I've confirmed"; A's possible line about buying with her husband; A's missing "why" for that concern. Withdrawn at A's request: the twin-assumption line — not recorded, nothing from it used anywhere.

Option 2, purchase by A only on explicitly agreed terms: after Option 1's facts, A and her husband may propose a purchase, with any price or terms — including or excluding a discount — discussed only after the effect on every share is visible and only with your explicit agreement. B's studio hope is taken seriously in considering how any proceeds are used within what the will allows; A's independence and wish to buy are not dismissed; all three may take independent advice, say no, and re-check this list before any documents are considered. If any of you says no, no purchase on those terms proceeds; the no is added as a need.
Option 3, all legally available alternatives, chosen only by explicit agreement: after the same shared facts, a neutral professional lays out the arrangements the will actually allows (for example, holding the house, a purchase, a third-party sale, or distribution) with the effect on each share; each sister explains at her own pace what matters to her; B's hope is not framed as taking from her sisters, A's wish to buy is not set aside without her say-so, and your share and clear agreement are required. You all re-check the list, add any new concerns, and only then say whether any arrangement meets every confirmed need. If none does, that is an acceptable outcome for now, recorded as unresolved.

Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with this? I'm asking A and B the same. Any no, even a small one, adds a need rather than a problem to overcome.
